c.tagline: New Zealand's Great Lake – geothermal steam, Huka Falls, and volcano trails.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis and a limited number of Uber drivers operate; book by phone or app, especially late at night when supply is thin.

emergency.note: 111 is New Zealand's single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Lock vehicles and hide valuables at trailhead and lakeside car parks, where opportunistic break-ins occur.

hood_desc: The compact, walkable heart on the lake's northern edge, packed with cafes, bars, the i-SITE and the marina where boat cruises and the Huka jet depart; best for first-timers who want everything on foot.
A relaxed lakeside strip a few minutes south of town with a swimming beach, the DeBretts hot pools nearby and easy reach of Huka Falls; suits couples and families wanting the lake without the bustle.
A quiet, upscale residential bay across the water with the area's best sunset lake-and-mountain views and sandy swimming beaches; a peaceful base with a car.
A leafy suburb just across the Control Gates Bridge and the Waikato River trails, walkable to town yet calmer; handy for cyclists and longer self-catered stays.
A resort-style village 20 minutes northwest with a sheltered marina and the Jack Nicklaus golf course, backed by the Great Lake Trail; suits golfers, boaties and hikers wanting seclusion.
lodging: Millennium Hotel and Resort Manuels Taupo

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Local bus and shuttle services run mainly in daytime; there is no night network, so most visitors drive or use taxis after hours.
transit.note: Taupō is a small lakeside town with no rail or tram; a compact local bus service plus taxis cover the town, but a car is by far the easiest way to reach Huka Falls, the Tongariro trailheads and the wider lake.
transit.pay: Local bus fares are paid in cash to the driver (a few dollars); there is no smartcard system.

bus: InterCity coaches to Auckland, Rotorua, Wellington and Napier

transit.m: Taxi or shuttle to the town centre (10-12 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not expected in New Zealand; staff are paid a full wage, though rounding up for exceptional service is welcome.
